title: Stage-1 contradiction fixes for supply coverage and live direction
summary: DDR v5.1 fixes two Stage 1 contradictions that could publish a No break signals verdict from unavailable supply evidence or a stale event direction. Stage 2, the sub-component versions and sealed predictions are unchanged.
impact: K1 supply weaponization and K4 reflexive death-spiral use the seven-day supply-change proxy only when mint-surge coverage is explicitly `supply-history-proxy` or null (legacy unmarked); an explicit `unavailable` coverage marker stays unavailable and cannot stand in for the hourly proxy.

An `above`-direction event whose live signed deviation is itself a below-peg break deeper than 1,000 bps is evaluated by the below-peg kill signals and tier mapping. A stale stored direction can no longer publish No break signals for a live deep break that its own depth readout already uses.

The resolution rubric, duration model, incident grouping, support rules and reviewer versions are unchanged; these fixes move only the affected new assessments and forecasts, and sealed predictions keep their original content, hashes and version stamps.
Activation is 2026-10-31 00:00 UTC (1793404800); no Stage 1 replay is claimed.

title: Evidence-class verdicts, competing-risk duration odds and reviewer v5
summary: DDR v5 condemns a coin only on terminal evidence, publishes duration as unconditional recovery odds that keep non-recovery visible, and grades its calls against naive baselines.
impact: Verdicts read as evidence classes: No break signals, Stress signals and Terminal evidence. Wire tier codes are unchanged; rows locked before v5 keep their original Recovery Likely / At Risk / Recovery Unlikely labels.

Static exit thinness no longer condemns a coin. V9 exit capacity is re-scaled from the Safety Score stress request (a $1M floor) to the dislocation's value gap, and it, no-viable-route and thin redemption capacity cap at elevated. K5 is severe only when DEX TVL collapses at least 40% from the event's onset baseline on a thin market.

Two or more elevated kill signals without a strong structural anchor are terminal evidence only on a severe below-peg break (deeper than 1,000 bps, using the worse of the stored peak and live deviation). A deep break with no kill signal reads as Stress signals.

Duration odds estimate the share of comparable incidents that recover, with terminal incidents as a competing outcome and still-open or non-recovery closures censored at their last observation (coin-weighted Aalen–Johansen). Quantiles the curve never reaches stay empty and the share not recovered within 30 days is published.
Typical-range and median readouts come from the incident-level curve instead of percentiles of per-coin medians. Horizon odds that fail the replay skill gate are published as not informative.

New predictions persist a raw decision-input snapshot so later methodology changes can be replayed over sealed history. Frozen v2–v4 predictions keep their contents, hashes and methodology; they are not regraded.
